commit_message:
[maglev] Improve constant handling for BuildCheckSmi and the Array ctor

This patch improves the handling of constants in two places in the
Maglev graph builder:

1. In `BuildCheckSmi`: We can now often avoid emitting a runtime smi
check if the input is a constant that is known to be a smi at compile
time.
2. In `TryReduceConstructArrayConstructor`: When determining the
elements kind for a newly constructed array, we can now extract type
information from constant arguments even if they don't have a precise
NodeType set. This allows for more accurate elements kind selection.

These changes should lead to slightly better code generation in cases
involving constants.

fix_commit.message: [maglev] Restrict BuildCheckSmi constant elision to non-tagged inputs
fix_commit.author: Jakob Linke

findings.title: BuildCheckSmi constant elision unsound for tagged inputs, allowing HeapNumber to bypass Smi check
findings.message:
MaglevGraphBuilder::BuildCheckSmi() added an optimization that skips emitting the runtime Smi check whenever TryGetInt32Constant(object) returns a value that lies within the Smi range (Smi::IsValid). This is only sound when the emitted check would have been a value-range check (e.g. for kInt32/kUint32/kFloat64/kHoleyFloat64/kIntPtr inputs, where the subsequently-emitted CheckInt32IsSmi/CheckUint32IsSmi/CheckFloat64IsSmi/CheckHoleyFloat64IsSmi/CheckIntPtrIsSmi checks are exactly what Smi::IsValid proves).

However, for kTagged inputs the runtime check that would otherwise be emitted is CheckSmi, which is a tag-bit check, not a value-range check. TryGetInt32Constant() can recurse through a node's 'checked_value' alternative, which BuildCheckNumericalValue's HeapNumber branch can populate with a Constant(HeapNumber N) after only a CheckFloat64SameValue (a numeric-equality check that both a Smi(N) and a HeapNumber(N) satisfy). Consequently, for a kTagged node whose alternative records a HeapNumber constant with a value in Smi range, BuildCheckSmi incorrectly elides the CheckSmi tag check and returns the object as though it were proven to be a Smi.

This allows a HeapNumber pointer to flow into code paths that assume a Smi (e.g. field stores using StoreTaggedFieldNoWriteBarrier because the field is believed to hold only Smis), producing a type confusion and a missing write barrier - a serious, exploitable memory-safety bug reachable from JavaScript via Maglev-compiled code.
findings.suggestion: Restrict the constant-value-based elision to non-tagged input representations, since only those cases have the following switch emit an equivalent value-range check. For kTagged inputs, rely only on the earlier type-system checks (StaticTypeIs(kSmi) / EnsureType(kSmi)) which correctly carry the tag guarantee; do not elide the CheckSmi tag check based on value-equivalence alone.

ground_truth.root_cause: The elision logic conflated numeric value-equivalence (proven by TryGetInt32Constant/Smi::IsValid) with Smi tagging. For non-tagged representations the two are equivalent because the fallback switch performs an explicit value-range check; but for kTagged inputs the fallback check (CheckSmi) verifies the pointer's tag bits, a distinct property not implied by numeric equivalence, especially since the 'checked_value' alternative can be populated with a HeapNumber constant purely from a same-value float comparison.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: BuildCheckSmi constant elision unsound for tagged inputs, allowing HeapNumber to bypass Smi check
